location: Boundaries > Always > Runner ('Exactly one record per admitted cell per run')
issue: The rule is stated without exceptions, but the contract (Evidence record > Storage) and the CAP-3 code (`_SlotRun._on_reaped`) leave NO record for the cells of a child that exits 2 or reports `status: skipped`, and after the first append error only reaped-child records are retried. So 'exactly one' is false for three paths that the spec itself keeps (the child-exit-2 interim rule depends on that child leaving no record).
implementation_impact: An implementer who writes the invariant test literally will either add records for exit-2/skipped children (breaking the contract and the existing `test_e2e_skipped`/exit-2 tests, and making a skipped child look like an inconclusive cell that the plan re-derives) or ship a test that fails on those paths.
suggestion: Reword as 'at most one record per admitted cell per run; exactly one unless the child exited 2, reported skipped, or an append error stopped appending', and list those three exceptions in the Stop/exit-2 tests.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner (stop path: 'children whose result is already in are reaped normally ... queued cells get no record, as today')
issue: Reaping normally goes through `_on_reaped`, which calls `_fire` on an appended `fail` (fail-fast) or on a child exit 2 (`input-error after <ver>`). `_fire` writes `not-run` records for every queued cell. So a child that finished with `fail` (or exit 2) just before the stop makes the stop path write `not-run` records for queued cells, which contradicts 'queued cells get no record'.
implementation_impact: Whether queued cells get `not-run` on a stop depends on timing. Tests become flaky, and a stopped run can leave `not-run` records saying `fail-fast after …` that the operator never caused.
suggestion: State that the stop path appends only the reaped child's own records and never triggers fail-fast or input-error `not-run` (a flag on `_on_reaped`). Or state explicitly that queued cells get `not-run` when a reaped result in the stop path is a `fail`/exit 2. Add a test with a done-but-unreaped failing future at stop time.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner (`stopped` records appended from the stop path)
issue: `JobStopped` is raised asynchronously from the SIGTERM handler (`_on_sigterm`) in the main thread, so it can land inside `_append` between `pl.append_record` (the line is already written) and `self.appended.append(...)`/`self.states.append(...)`. It can also land partway through a multi-engine child's records. The spec does not say how the stop path knows which cells already got their record.
implementation_impact: The stop path can write a second, newer `stopped` record for a cell whose real result was just appended. That breaks 'exactly one record per run'. Because `cell_reason` reads the newest fresh record, it also turns that cell's rerun reason from `fail` into `inconclusive`, so the plan and the infra-retry prompt misreport an operator stop as an infra problem.
suggestion: Require the stop to be deferred around record writes (for example `signal.pthread_sigmask` blocking SIGTERM across append plus bookkeeping, or a handler that sets a flag checked between appends). Track 'written' per cell, not per version. Add a test that injects the stop between two engines' appends.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (interim rule: 'before an infra retry (re-running a step whose previous run left an infra cause ...)')
issue: No deterministic signal for 'the previous run left an infra cause' is defined. The plan's e2e `rerun_matrix` reason collapses every inconclusive record to `inconclusive`, whether its reason is `crash`, `no-slots`, `browser-unavailable` or `stopped` (which the contract says is not an infra cause). `e2e_blocked_causes` is `{}` outside `blocked-*`. The interim 'Run outcomes' definition, which said where the cause comes from, is not among the four rules carried over, and the interim file is replaced as a whole.
implementation_impact: After an individually stopped child (exit 1, `stopped` records) or a rerun Budi requested after exit 143, the orchestrator sees `inconclusive` and prompts Budi to fix the environment for what was an operator stop. For a real infra cause, it has no cause name to report unless it parses stderr or the histories ad hoc.
suggestion: Either have the plan emit the cause additively (for example `cause` on e2e `rerun_matrix` entries = the newest non-`stopped` record's infra cause, null otherwise), or define in the docs that an infra retry is due when a cell in `e2e_next_cells` has a newest non-`stopped` record with an infra cause, read from the records listed in the run's `appended`. Either way, `stopped` must not trigger the environment prompt.

location: Boundaries > Always > Plan (`clean` via ps-aggregate layer functions) and Design Notes > `clean` ('a per-version file that does not load or fails validate_layer_shape = exit 2 naming it')
issue: The exit-2 rule is not limited to versions whose `phase1_reuse` is already true. `plan_layer` today treats an unreadable or truncated per-version file as `rerun` ('file lapis tak terbaca'), which is the recovery path after a killed Layer 2/5 run. Under this wording the plan exits 2 on that same file before the orchestrator can rerun the layer. The E2E plan call (operator scope, every in-scope version) also loads other versions' files, so one broken 1.7.8 file blocks the hosting loop of 9.1.
implementation_impact: A Layer 2 run killed mid-write leaves psm-validate stuck: every per-version plan call exits 2, and the orchestrator has no plan output telling it to rerun the layer.
suggestion: Specify that `clean` short-circuits to false without loading any file when `per_version[V].phase1_reuse` is false. Load and validate shape only for fresh files (`reuse: true`), and add a test where a truncated stale per-version file yields `clean: false` with exit 0.

issue: `--tier` becomes mandatory (exit 2 when missing) for every non-merge-only `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e` run. The command examples that must change are in `references/run-phases.md` (Fase 1 and Fase 2 blocks), `references/e2e-quickstart.md`, the SKILL.md Lapis 4 paragraph and the ps-run-layer docstring example (line ~89). Verification only runs unit tests plus one manual headless check, so nothing catches a stale example without `--tier`, a leftover `--jobs`, or the 'Istilah E2E (interim, sampai CAP-1)' heading surviving.
implementation_impact: One missed example makes the model-driven orchestrator emit a command that exits 2 pre-spawn. Under the interim rules that is 'fix and rerun' interactively but `blocked` in headless, so every headless caller can be blocked by a doc typo.
suggestion: Add mechanical doc checks to Verification, for example: every `--layer e2e` command line in `.claude/skills/**/*.md` and the ps-run-layer docstring that is not `--merge-only` contains `--tier`; no 'interim, sampai CAP-1' text remains; the interim companion carries the superseded note.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (hosting version / run scope) and contract Docs to update > 'On Activation: step 2 scope'
issue: Any interactive run scope that excludes the current focus cell (on a fresh or clean-after-patch module, any scope without the canary version or browser, e.g. 'only 1.7.8') makes the very first E2E plan call `blocked-by-scope`. That ends the E2E loop with zero runs. The spec does not require the scope menu to warn about this, so narrowing reads as 'test 1.7.8' but silently means 'test nothing E2E'.
implementation_impact: Budi narrows scope to save time, waits through Layers 1/2/5, and only learns at the report that no browser ran. Fixing it costs a new session.
suggestion: Require the On Activation step 2 text, and the scope menu's summary, to state that E2E runs only when the scope contains the current focus cell (canary by default), and to show the plan's `e2e_focus_cell`/`e2e_required_cells` before Budi confirms a narrowed scope.

location: Boundaries > Always > Canary ('any other value or a cell outside the configured set = exit 2 in plan, aggregate ...')
issue: The plan validates the canary on every call, including the Phase 1 per-version calls that only gate Layers 1/2/5, and the aggregate validates it even with `--require` excluding `e2e` or `psm_e2e_enabled` false. An explicit `psm_e2e_canary` left over after editing `psm_target_versions` (e.g. dropping 9.1) therefore blocks the whole validation, including modules with E2E disabled. The spec does not say what the error must tell the operator.
implementation_impact: Interactive psm-validate becomes unusable after a routine target-version edit, with an exit 2 whose cause (an E2E-only key) is not obvious from a Layer 1 plan call. Headless is shielded only by the config-copy reset.
suggestion: Require the exit-2 message to name `psm_e2e_canary`, its value and the configured cells, with the fix (clear it or pick a configured cell). Have On Activation validate it once up front. Under Ask First, decide whether validation should be skipped when `psm_e2e_enabled` is false.

location: I/O & Edge-Case Matrix, row 'Clean module' ('aggregate `ready` true')
issue: Aggregate `ready` needs every required layer. The default `--require` is all four layers, and `version_ready` also needs `m['pass']` and the static conclusiveness floor (`rules_evaluated` > 0, main file found) regardless of `--require`. The row specifies only E2E histories, so the test cannot reach `ready: true` without unstated Layer 1/2/3/5 fixtures, or a `--require` choice the row does not give.
implementation_impact: The implementer either builds an ad hoc multi-layer fixture or weakens the assertion. The CAP-1 success claim ('with a clean module ... ready is true') ends up tested against an undefined setup.
suggestion: Pin the setup: `--require e2e` plus a minimal conclusive static fixture (rules_evaluated ≥ 1, main_file_found true). Or assert the E2E part only: all six `e2e_cells` gate-grade `pass`, every `versions[V].layers.e2e.conclusive` true, and no e2e `inconclusive_note`.

location: Tasks > tests ('CAP-3 expectations "SIGTERM'd child → no record" become `stopped`') and I/O row 'Stop'
issue: The existing stop test (`test_e2e_stopped`) injects the stop as the result of the 9.1 child's future (`fut.result()` raising `JobStopped`) with `--slots 1`, so at most one child is ever in flight. The new behaviour, `stopped` appended for every other in-flight admitted cell 'without waiting for the children', and results already in being reaped normally, cannot be exercised by that harness.
implementation_impact: The stop path can ship with only the trivial single-child case covered. The multi-child cases (one sibling still running, one done but unreaped, one just admitted) are exactly where duplicates or missing records appear.
suggestion: Specify a test with `--slots ≥ 3` and three admitted versions: one done and reaped, one done but unreaped, one blocked in its runner. Raise `JobStopped` from the main loop (e.g. a stubbed `wait`), and assert exactly one record per admitted cell, `stopped` only for the unfinished one, no record for queued cells, exit 143, and no output line.

location: Acceptance Criteria #2 ('Given config 3×2 and `--versions 9.1 --browsers chromium` ... `rerun_matrix` still lists the other five cells')
issue: The criterion has no history precondition. `rerun_matrix` lists a cell only when it lacks passing gate-grade evidence, so with passing histories for those five cells the expected output is wrong. The criterion also does not say that the 9.1:chromium entry itself is unaffected by scope.
implementation_impact: A test author has to guess the fixture, and the test may pass vacuously on an empty reports dir without proving that the scope filter does not touch `rerun_matrix`.
suggestion: Add the precondition ('with no history', or 'all six cells stale-source'). Assert that `rerun_matrix` e2e entries are identical with and without `--versions 9.1 --browsers chromium`, while only `e2e_next_cells` differs.
